spine: 1. 起點：最忙的 repository 一秒最多幾十次寫入且多為突發，作者預期一年內變成持續速率，目標設為至少多兩個數量級，且每次 push 帶出更多讀取。
2. 支點：Git 物件不可變、可並行寫入，只有 reference 更新需要共識，所以儲存、服務、維護可以各自獨立擴充。
3. 兩次卡在 blob 的嘗試：單一 blob 的 write-ahead log 寫入落在每秒數百次的中間水準；拆 segment 提高寫入上限卻讓讀取要查全部 segment。
4. Ref-CAS：quorum 提交的 compare-and-swap，只鎖碰到的 reference，版本是最新 LSN，版本相同時讀取只花一次比較，且只存指標、不存物件資料。
5. Rubicon 資料平面：Spokes 沿用，virtual replica 是可丟棄的運算，物件在 Blob Storage，compaction 移到背景獨立節點。
6. Compaction 流程：lease、open segment、封口、合併、驗證、兩筆交易；以 pack 雜湊分 shard 並分層合併，使 pack 數量在 push 上升時大致持平。
7. 收斂與缺口：目標是一套架構服務所有 repository；後續工作分架構、agent 操作、Git 本身三塊；文章沒給 commit 延遲數字與測試條件細節，目前為 limited private preview，更廣推出在明年初。

perspective.mechanism: 只有 reference 更新需要共識：reference 放在 quorum 提交、逐 reference 加鎖的 Ref-CAS 日誌，物件放 Blob Storage，virtual replica 是可丟棄的快取運算，compaction 由獨立節點透過 lease 與 shard 在背景完成。
perspective.tradeoff: 單一 blob 日誌讀便宜但寫入受限於每次往返一次條件式寫入；拆 segment 提高寫入上限卻把成本轉到讀取。Ref-CAS 引入專用共識群組，換得逐 reference 排序與一次比較的讀取。
perspective.reader_use: 台灣的後端或基礎設施工程師可以拿它檢查自己的系統：哪一小塊狀態真的需要共識、物件儲存的條件式寫入當序列化點的上限在哪、維護工作能否搬出服務節點。

notes.quote: Through internal testing, we’ve demonstrated the ability to support 5,000 concurrent agents working on a repository, sending 7,200 pushes per second to a repo, all while serving read traffic with consistently low latency.
notes.interpretation: 數字來自內部測試，不是公開基準；文章沒有交代 repo 大小、push 大小、衝突比例。

notes.quote: Git objects are immutable and named by their contents, meaning two writers can store them at the same time without agreeing on anything. The part of a push that needs agreement is the reference update, and a reference update is tiny in comparison.
notes.interpretation: 整個設計的支點，也是上一篇留下的觀察。

notes.quote: Only reference updates need agreement. That lets the parts of Git infrastructure that used to be tightly coupled (storing data, serving requests, and maintaining repositories) scale independently.
notes.interpretation: 三件事可獨立擴充，是文章對設計結果的主張。

notes.quote: Today, the busiest repositories on GitHub.com receive at most dozens of writes in a single second, typically in short bursts.
notes.interpretation: 現況基準：最忙的 repo 也只是每秒幾十次寫入。

notes.quote: As more of that work shifts to agents running in parallel and around the clock, we expect those bursts to become a sustained rate within the next year.
notes.interpretation: 作者的預期，不是已發生的事實；文中以「作者預期」呈現。

notes.quote: The chart below shows daily requests to one repository on GitHub from March to May, when its traffic grew about 4x. Its growth has continued on an exponential trajectory since then.
notes.interpretation: 單一頂端 repo 的例子；原文附圖，本文沒有引用圖上數值。

notes.quote: Instead of planning for the next increment, we set a target of at least two orders of magnitude more scale.
notes.interpretation: 目標是至少多兩個數量級。

notes.quote: Experience has taught us that indexing incoming packs and checking object connectivity are the most CPU-expensive parts of a write, and that cost scales with the size of the write, so a single node will become compute-bound quickly.
notes.interpretation: 需要多個 writer 節點的第一個理由。

notes.quote: Spreading that work across many nodes improves fault tolerance and shortens recovery when a node fails.
notes.interpretation: 第二個理由：容錯與恢復。

notes.quote: Minimize commit latency. An agent waits on each push before it moves to its next step.
notes.interpretation: 需求之一；文章全篇沒有給 commit 延遲的具體數字。

notes.quote: Keep reads cheap when nothing has changed, which is the common case given the read-to-write ratio.
notes.interpretation: 需求之一，對應 LSN 版本檢查。

notes.quote: On top of that, the system had to be able to improve overall reliability and scale globally.
notes.interpretation: 六條單一 repo 需求之外的整體要求。

notes.quote: In May of 2026, hot on the heels of the initial Azure migration, we started working on a design that could meet those demands. We tried several approaches.
notes.interpretation: 設計工作的起點與時間點。

notes.quote: In all of them, pack data lived in Azure Blob Storage, and in some we experimented with keeping reference state there too.
notes.interpretation: 各種嘗試的共同點。

notes.quote: We called it “Rubicon,” a nod to the point of no return the industry crossed with agentic development.
notes.interpretation: 命名由來。

notes.quote: requests from Git clients, the API, and the web UI arrive at Spokes, which still handles routing and load balancing, and serves the internal API that the rest of GitHub uses to read and write repository data.
notes.interpretation: Spokes 沿用既有角色。

notes.quote: Virtual replicas are a single fleet of disposable compute that serves reads, writes, or both. A virtual replica’s local disk is a cache that can be rebuilt at any time.
notes.interpretation: virtual replica 是可丟棄的運算，本地磁碟只是快取。

notes.quote: Spokes routes a repository’s traffic to the same virtual replicas when it can, which keeps their caches warm and latency low, but nothing about correctness depends on a request landing on any particular virtual replica.
notes.interpretation: 路由偏好只影響快取熱度，不影響正確性。

notes.quote: When a repository gets busy, we add more virtual replicas.
notes.interpretation: 擴充方式。

notes.quote: That work never runs on a virtual replica, meaning their CPU and memory can be almost entirely dedicated to serving requests.
notes.interpretation: compaction 不在 replica 上跑，replica 資源留給請求。

notes.quote: References and the list of packs that make up the repository (the pack manifest) live in a separate replicated log service we call Ref-CAS (for “Reference Compare-and-Swap”).
notes.interpretation: Ref-CAS 的定位。

notes.quote: a virtual replica indexes the incoming pack and uploads it to Blob Storage, then commits one transaction to Ref-CAS that lists the pack in the manifest and updates the references.
notes.interpretation: 寫入路徑。

notes.quote: a virtual replica checks its reference version with Ref-CAS, pulls the packs it needs from Blob Storage into its cache, and serves the read from there.
notes.interpretation: 讀取路徑。

notes.quote: Most of that data is written once to a distinct key and never changes afterward, which is what makes it highly suitable for Blob Storage.
notes.interpretation: 物件類資料適合物件儲存的原因。

notes.quote: Checkpoints for the reference state of the repository, though not the authoritative state used to serve requests.
notes.interpretation: Blob Storage 上的 reference checkpoint 不是權威狀態。

notes.quote: References are the opposite. A busy repository’s references are a relatively small piece of state that many writes race to update at the same time.
notes.interpretation: reference 與物件資料的存取型態相反。

notes.quote: Our first approach was a write-ahead log for all of a repository’s references, indexed by a single blob. Every update is a conditional write against that blob.
notes.interpretation: 第一個嘗試。

notes.quote: Only one conditional write to a blob can be in flight at a time, so even when we batch every push that arrives during a write into the next one, the repository’s write ceiling is one write per round trip to a single blob. In practice, this netted us write throughput in the mid-hundreds per second.
notes.interpretation: 單一 blob 方案的寫入上限與實測量級。

notes.quote: Our second approach split the references across several segment blobs, with each reference hashing to one of them. Writes to references in different segments no longer wait on each other, which raises the ceiling. But a read now has to check every segment to know whether anything changed, and it’s only as fast as the slowest segment. We’d traded write latency for read latency, and reads outnumber writes by orders of magnitude.
notes.interpretation: 第二個嘗試與其取捨。

notes.quote: This is the (small) consensus group we said at the end of the last post was still somewhere in the stack.
notes.interpretation: Ref-CAS 對應上一篇結尾提到的小型共識群組。

notes.quote: A transaction locks only the references it touches, checks that each one still has the value the writer expects, and becomes visible once a majority of the log’s replicas have recorded it. Agents mostly push to their own branches, so most updates don’t contend, and they replicate in parallel. When two pushes do update the same reference, only one will append to the log.
notes.interpretation: Ref-CAS 的交易規則。

notes.quote: Each commit to Ref-CAS gets a log sequence number (LSN), and the repository’s version is the LSN of its latest commit.
notes.interpretation: 版本即最新 LSN。

notes.quote: If that version is still current, the reply carries no references at all, and an unchanged repository costs a single comparison. If the virtual replica is behind, it gets back the current references and version, along with pointers to pack data and anything else that needs to be known, such as when the last garbage collection cycle occurred.
notes.interpretation: 讀取的版本檢查機制。

notes.quote: Unlike the consensus group in our legacy architecture, Ref-CAS never holds or validates object data. It only stores pointers to it. A virtual replica uploads a push’s pack to Blob Storage before it commits the reference transaction. A reference only ever points at objects that are already durable.
notes.interpretation: Ref-CAS 只存指標，且 pack 先上傳再提交。

notes.quote: These approaches allow us to transact reference state alone in the tens of thousands of operations per second, and provide a baseline for additional annotations on the replication log that help reads decide what to download for a given request.
notes.interpretation: 單算 reference 狀態每秒數萬次操作；與 7,200 pushes 不是同一個量。

notes.quote: In our legacy architecture, compaction runs on the same replicas that serve traffic, and it has to run on every replica.
notes.interpretation: 舊架構的 compaction 配置。

notes.quote: Git can serve a repository from many packs, but each additional pack makes lookups slightly more expensive, so the pack count can’t grow without bound.
notes.interpretation: 為何需要 compaction。

notes.quote: Compaction nodes each claim ownership over a subset of the repository’s data via a lease, which allows us to scale compaction horizontally.
notes.interpretation: lease 讓 compaction 可水平擴充。

notes.quote: The node first takes a lease on the shard in Blob Storage, so only one node compacts a shard at a time.
notes.interpretation: 步驟一。

notes.quote: When the segment reaches a defined limit based on pack count, size, or age, it seals the segment so it accepts no new packs, then combines its packs into fewer, larger ones. While compaction happens, the next segment for the shard can begin capturing its input packs.
notes.interpretation: 封口條件與下一個 segment 同時收 pack。

notes.quote: Before anything is published, the node checks that the new packs contain exactly the same objects as the inputs. It then uploads the new packs and adds them to the manifest. A second transaction removes the inputs from the manifest, and cleanup deletes them later.
notes.interpretation: 驗證、加入、移除三步；兩段式的好處是本文的推斷，原文未明說。

notes.quote: Each pack’s hash maps to a shard, so adding shards and nodes adds compaction throughput. A compacted pack that’s still under the size limit goes back into a shard by its own hash and merges again, so packs grow in tiers until they reach the limit. The net result is an effectively flat pack count while pushes climb:
notes.interpretation: shard 與分層合併使 pack 數量持平；原文以圖呈現，本文未引用圖上數值。

notes.quote: Compaction merges packs, but it keeps every object. Garbage collection is the step that removes objects nothing references anymore, like the ones left behind by deleted branches and force-pushes.
notes.interpretation: compaction 與垃圾回收的分工。

notes.quote: It also has a few special behaviors for safely removing data, which are worthy of their own discussion.
notes.interpretation: 垃圾回收的特殊行為留待另文。

notes.quote: Using these approaches, we’ve been able to consistently demonstrate a flat latency curve as writes climb, and we have other planned optimizations to make the compaction and garbage collection processes themselves more performant.
notes.interpretation: 只有定性的延遲描述，沒有數字。

notes.quote: Our goal is for every repository, from one developer’s side project to the busiest monorepo, to run on the same architecture with no special handling for the busy ones.
notes.interpretation: 單一架構的目標。

notes.quote: Read only what’s needed. Fetch a single object from Blob Storage instead of the whole pack that holds it.
notes.interpretation: 計畫中的改進（We have plans），非已上線。

notes.quote: Atomic commit API. Land a multi-file change in one operation. The whole change commits, or it’s rejected cleanly on conflict.
notes.interpretation: fast-follow 項目，非已上線。

notes.quote: Metadata like the commit-graph can answer merge-base and reachability questions without walking every commit.
notes.interpretation: 更快的歷史走訪方向。

notes.quote: It’s available in a limited private preview now, with a broader rollout early next year.
notes.interpretation: 上線狀態與時程；以文章發表日 2026-11-05 為基準。

notes.quote: For developers, Git stays Git: they push, fetch, and branch the same way, with the same protections in place.
notes.interpretation: 對開發者的相容性承諾。

notes.quote: Last week at GitHub Universe, we announced our new Git storage architecture, capable of handling thousands of writes per second with reads that scale on demand.
notes.interpretation: 文章開頭交代架構是在 GitHub Universe 公布，本文發表於其後一週。

notes.quote: Karthik Raman & Brian Celenza
notes.interpretation: 文章署名作者。

notes.quote: November 5, 2026
notes.interpretation: 文章標示的發表日期。
